Intent Process parcels or inventory updates spread across several arrays or maps. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. Positional counting continues across the outer collection sequence. Non-array/non-map input is XPTY0141. Map entry ordering is not an application sorting contract. ## 5. Motivation Process parcels or inventory updates spread across several arrays or maps. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Nested loops that flatten array members can destroy a parcel boundary. Map entry order should not be treated as stable business order; explicitly sort when presentation order matters. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(for member $parcel in ([('FILTER-A','BOLT-M8')], ['MANUAL']) return string(count($parcel)), ',') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences The initial REQ-118 stability table deferred sequences of arrays/maps, but S4 shipped this extension. for member binds complete array members, including multi-item sequences; for key/value binds map entries. Positional counting continues across the outer collection sequence. Non-array/non-map input is XPTY0141. Map entry ordering is not an application sorting contract. Nested loops that flatten array members can destroy a parcel boundary. Map entry order should not be treated as stable business order; explicitly sort when presentation order matters. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [arrays.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/arrays.xpath): returns `2,1` at mode 40. [maps.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/maps.xpath): returns `BOLT-M8=5,FILTER-A=2` at mode 40. [invalid.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/invalid.xpath): raises `XPTY0141` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `sequence-collection-iteration-arrays`, `sequence-collection-iteration-maps`, `sequence-collection-iteration-invalid`. [`Evaluate_ForMember_SequenceOfArraysCountsPositionsAcrossArrays`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ForKeyValue_PositionalCountsAcrossMaps`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Intent Construct a changed record while keeping its declared field constraints and leaving the original value available. ## 3. Also Known As A ButWithExpr performs a record update by construction. History / Supersedes A 3.1 adapter can select/validate fields, convert values and create a replacement map with map:merge/use-last. The [complete baseline](../examples/record-contracts/report-3.xsl) does that for the stock task. It has no record annotation and is not a universal replacement for record coercion. [The 4.0 report](../examples/record-contracts/report-4.xsl) casts the imported map, then constructs its amended record. ## 5. Motivation A stock feed supplies quantity and delta. The report must show both the imported quantity and adjusted quantity, preserve row order and reject invalid lexical numbers. Record update makes a changed typed value explicit while retaining the before value. [Complete input/output and repair contract](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) makes the task independently runnable. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath's annotation-driven reconstruction, not JavaScript object spread or an unrestricted immutable dictionary update. Undeclared fields and noncoercible values fail. A cast may discard surplus keys and convert a lexical string to an integer; update uses coercion and therefore does not automatically perform that lexical cast. Optional empty values are entries whose values are empty, not absent keys. Structural records are distinct from XSLT-defined nominal identity. ## 7. Applicability Use it after establishing the target record annotation. At import boundaries, deliberately select cast versus coercion: cast filters extras; coercion rejects them. Supply correctly typed update values or convert them explicitly. The stock task casts @delta to integer before updating qty. This example permits negative adjustments and does not enforce a nonnegative-stock rule. ## 8. Structure ```xpath ((map{'a':1} cast as record(a as xs:integer)) but with map{'a':2})?a ``` This is the runnable `record-contract-update-value` probe and returns2. The original-preservation probe produces `1|2` from before/after lookups. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) handles record syntax and but-with expressions. [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) applies the existing annotation/coercion path. [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) and the public [documentation runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) provide named evidence; no new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations Cast constructs the import record, adding a present-but-empty optional note and dropping import-only trace. Update merges the replacement quantity and recoerces to the left annotation. The output keeps the original quantity and adjusted value in a row map. Map access and record lookup are distinct: map:get can inspect a missing key without the record lookup's undeclared-field error. ## 11. Consequences Unknown fields, a plain-map left operand, a non-map right operand and an empty required field raise XPTY0004 in the supplied probes. Integer-to-double promotion is checked; arbitrary string-to-integer update casting is not implied. Optional fields may be set to empty while retaining key presence. Nested structural conversion and declaration order are bounded tested cases, not proof of every composite/nominal type combination. ## 12. Implementation **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Annotation-preserving reconstruction retains the original value; Unknown fields, plain-map left operand and invalid replacement values refuse; Optional empty values retain key presence; nested promotion and field order are bounded. **Boundary:** Update uses coercion, not lexical import casting. Structural examples do not establish every nominal static/default-field update, method or package context. Ownership: T04, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Thirty-five XPath probes cover cast/coercion/update distinctions; three explicit 3.1 refusal cases and eight complete3.0/4.0 reports bring the slice to46 documentation checks. The first run exposed a record-signature gate leak in old profiles, separate from value semantics. [The parser finding](../INLINE-RECORD-TYPE-GATE.md) and 44 dedicated API regressions preserve the failures and bounded correction. The new examples do not invent or promote a qt4 gate. ## 13. Sample Code The [complete report](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) uses `` and yields `BOLT:10->12|NUT:4->3|items=2;total=15` in both versions. Empty input yields `items=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid delta `oops` raises FORG0001. No external variables or resources are needed. Report stylesheets specify namespaces and all context. ## 14. Performance Notes Reconstruction checks declared fields and may recursively convert nested values; it can allocate a new record and entries. The report retains before/after values and is not a streaming/persistence benchmark. No speed or memory advantage over the baseline is claimed; use the benchmark harness for measured workloads. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `record-contract-update-value`, `record-contract-update-original`, `record-contract-update-annotation`, `record-contract-update-extra`, `record-contract-update-promote`, `record-contract-update-empty-optional` and the report cases, all enumerated in [the slice audit](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json), run by CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome. [InlineRecordTypeVersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/InlineRecordTypeVersionGateTests.cs) independently verifies44 version/signature controls. No feature-specific qt4 gated-set assignment is made. Historical upstream RecordType fixtures reflect an older draft; named tests and executable examples are explicit applicable evidence, not whole-suite conformance or automatic AC-03 closure. ## 16. XSLT 4.0 union minimum priority

Source 1.23.3 assigns a 4.0 node-union template the **minimum** default priority of its alternatives, including alternatives that do not match the current item. Public 1.23.2 uses the maximum. EQNAME-BRACKET-PARSING.md.text:
EQName bracket parsing

22 October 2026 - source 1.23.5, unpublished

**Public1.23.7 - 23 October2026:** EQName bracket parsing, inline-record signature gates and numeric separator boundaries are [published and verified](../RELEASE-1.23.7-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## Contract and finding The [XPath 3.1 BracedURILiteral grammar](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-31/#doc-xpath31-BracedURILiteral) excludes curly braces from the literal content, not square brackets. Namespace validation may optionally reject invalid URI values; this correction retains Bosak's permissive namespace-literal policy. The [current draft grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), production `BracedURILiteral` for `xslt40-patterns`, has the same square-bracket boundary. Upstream master was refreshed on 22 October 2026 to `b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c`; this is a current review pin, not recovered historical adoption. Immutable grammar and XSLT XML copies are retained with validation receipts. Before the correction, `Q{urn:n[part]}root` was split at the namespace's opening bracket as though it started a predicate. All 32 initial transformation regressions failed on the unmodified engine, in both effective 3.0 and 4.0 profiles. A URI containing an unmatched opening square bracket is also literal content: the closing curly brace ends the namespace literal. ## Implementation `PatternCompiler.FindPredicateStart` scans outside EQName namespace literals and quoted strings, including doubled quote escapes. Single-step element and attribute dispatch, path ancestor/final-step classification, and predicate extraction use the same boundary. Actual predicates after the EQName still use the existing matcher, sibling focus and delimiter handling. This is an internal XSLT pattern correction; the XPath lexer and public API are unchanged. End-to-end tests use explicit template priorities to isolate matching from dispatch priority. They cover exact names and nonmatches, unmatched URI square brackets, attributes and explicit axes, kind tests, wildcard names, union and parenthesized patterns, ancestor/final-step predicates, nested EQNames within real predicates, positional and chained predicates, and both 3.0/4.0 profiles. The newly supported names also exposed a remaining raw bracket check in effective 4.0 default-priority classification. With parsing fixed but the original priority check retained, both new opening-bracket priority cases fail while eight existing URI punctuation cases pass. That check now uses the already URI-masked name, giving an expanded-name test priority 0 rather than predicate priority 0.5. Earlier-profile default-priority classification remains unchanged, as in the 1.23.4 correction; this slice does not claim exhaustive earlier-profile URI-punctuation priorities. There are **44 new matching cases plus two new 4.0 priority cases**. All **159 focused checks pass**, including existing delimiter, EQName-priority and union/set-priority regressions. Full-suite and gate results are recorded in [the machine-readable audit](EQNAME-BRACKET-PARSING.json). Final validation: **10,516 solution tests pass**, including **7,548 XSLT tests**, with no failures or skips. QT3 stays **31,142/0/679** and qt4 gated stays **8,278/0/1,894**. Release build succeeds with zero errors and ten NU1900 warnings because NuGet vulnerability metadata was unavailable; the authorized restore retry retained those warnings. No successful vulnerability audit is claimed. Temporary worktree fixture junctions were removed after validation, leaving the shared catalogs unchanged. The original red run, intermediate attempts and successful runs are retained under `.guard-tmp/req126-eqname-parser-evidence`. ## Delivery and remaining scope Base: `0f1c4b2158235bb92dd62ea3aed645efcd9a8879` (main after PR #408). Source 1.23.5 is unpublished; public release remains 1.23.4. No Braid dependency or acceptance change is included. REQ-126 remains In Progress; D2/D3/D4 and AC-03 remain partial. Catalog manifests and worked reports retain 71 entries, 2,743 feature plus 24 chapter checks, four chapters and 117 assigned function names. These new engine regressions are separate from catalog check counts. Older opening-bracket limitations in [the 1.23.4 priority delivery](EQNAME-PATTERN-PRIORITY.md) describe the earlier source and remain historical evidence.

That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). This page covers zero-argument constructors. For `fn { ... }`, `function { ... }`, the `fn(...)` abbreviation and pipeline focus, use the separate [focus-function syntax entry](focus-function-syntax.md). Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, call xs:integer(.) explicitly. The receiving system requires typed values; the import report exposes canonical values before accepting the delivery. Use the current item as the argument to a zero-arity constructor inside a simple map. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. There must be a suitable focus, and invalid lexical data still fails; this is conversion, not validation. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. There must be a suitable focus, and invalid lexical data still fails; this is conversion, not validation. ## 8. Consequences Benefit: Use the current item as the argument to a zero-arity constructor inside a simple map. There must be a suitable focus, and invalid lexical data still fails; this is conversion, not validation. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-focus. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies All 49 registered zero-arity names with representative lexical conversion, type/error and context checks; Direct/reference/lookup/node paths, explicit one-argument comparison, empty iteration and missing focus; QName static namespace and captured-focus boundaries. **Boundary:** A zero-arity constructor requires suitable focus; empty simple-map input invokes nothing. xs:error has no nonempty successful value, and its empty/type fixture is not proof of a constructed value. Representative inputs do not certify all facets, namespaces, schema types or arbitrary casts. Ownership: T03, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code The introductory input is declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/focus-functions/main.xpath) yields `12,5`. The [edge case](../examples/focus-functions/edge.xpath) yields `FORG0001 (expected error)`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ### Supplier delivery import and constructor audit The [detailed example README](../examples/focus-functions/README.md) explains full input/output, field responsibilities, failures and compatibility. It links every published file and the [49-name audit inventory](../audit-focus-constructors.json). The new audit adds **508 executable checks** (including representative types, context/error/cardinality cases, 3.1 alternatives and experimental outcomes); the original three checks remain. Input: ```xml ``` Complete [4.0 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-40.xpath): ```xquery string-join(for $line in parse-xml('')/deliveries/line return concat($line/@id, '|', $line/@quantity ! xs:integer(), '|', $line/@price ! xs:decimal(), '|', $line/@date ! xs:date(), '|', $line/@active ! xs:boolean()), ';') ``` Output (id, quantity, price, promised date, active flag): ```text A|12|2.5|2026-10-12|true;B|5|4|2026-10-13|false ``` The [3.1 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-31.xpath) uses explicit `(.)` constructor arguments and produces identical output. Mapping two lexical inputs invokes the constructor once per item: scalar types produce two values; ENTITIES/IDREFS/NMTOKENS produce four for two two-token inputs. Default argument is the context item; list/union contracts remain distinct. This current comparison does not recover the historically adopted pin. Source: [generated registrations and XsFocusCtor](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); coercion: [VM engine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs). ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: per-item conversion. Invalid values still require error classification rather than a successful result. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `focus-functions-main`, `focus-functions-edge`, `focus-functions-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.m.text:
Destructuring let

Catalog entry — Operators & syntax · Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Destructuring `let` bindings** — **Frozen 4.0** (ships at the `XPath40` level; static XPST0003 at `XPath31`). Spec: XPath 4.0 §4.14 (FLWOR expressions), [QT4CG PR #1131](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/1131). Landed: REQ-123 destructuring-let cluster, [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129) (main `b8e4b9f`, 2026-10-10). **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: let expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-let-expressions). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129), [immutable mainline revision `b8e4b9f5`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/b8e4b9f510543c04d88a7c10ee2af28808a0fd5c) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Bind several variables at once by decomposing a sequence, an array, or a map on the right-hand side — `let $($x, $y) := (1, 2)` binds `$x` to `1` and `$y` to `2` in one clause, evaluating the right-hand side exactly once. ## 3. Also Known As "Destructuring binding" (spec), "tuple binding" (informal, from the tuple-builder relative). Not to be confused with the `for` clause's *tuple* destructuring, which is a separate (larger) construct. ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind: | Before (3.1) | After (4.0) | |---|---| | `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind | | `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` | | `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names | ## 5. Motivation The 3.1 idioms are error-prone in two ways: the RHS is visually repeated (or manually hoisted into a helper variable, cluttering scope), and positional indexing silently does the wrong thing when the sequence is shorter than expected. Destructuring makes the arity contract explicit and puts the shape of the data next to the names it feeds. ## 6. Language Alignment Prior art: ML/Haskell pattern bindings, ES6 `const {a, b} = obj` / `const [x, y] = arr`. **Semantic drift — read before relying on intuition:** - The **last variable of a sequence pattern takes all remaining items** (`let $($x, $y) := (1,2,3)` → `$y = (2,3)`); ES6 array destructuring instead discards surplus elements. Surplus *variables* (too few items) bind `()`. - The **array form is strict about surplus**: `let $[$a, $b] := [1,2,3]` discards member 3, but too few members for the variables is **FOAY0001**, not `undefined`-style filling. - The **map form binds by variable name** (`${$name}` looks up key `"name"`), closer to ES6 object destructuring than to map lookup — but a missing key binds `()` rather than throwing. ## 7. Applicability Use for: unpacking fixed-shape sequences/arrays/maps at the head of a FLWOR; replacing two-or-more positional `let`s over the same value. Do **not** use for: library expressions that must still compile at `XPath31` (static XPST0003); one-item unpacks (`let $x := $seq[1]` remains clearer); hot loops where the save/restore cost (§14) matters and the 3.1 form was already hoisted. ## 8. Structure ``` LetBinding ::= SimpleLetBinding | DestructuringLetBinding DestructuringLetBinding ::= "$" ("(" | "[" | "{") VariableSpec ("," VariableSpec)* (")" | "]" | "}") TypeDeclaration? ":=" ExprSingle VariableSpec ::= "$" VarName (TypeDeclaration)? (* per-variable type, optional *) ``` Three bracket kinds select the source container: `(` sequence, `[` single array, `{` single map. ## 9. Participants - `XPathParser.ParseDestructuringLetBinding` — parses all three kinds; gated on the parser's xpath40 flag; empty pattern → XPST0003. - `XPathAstNode.LetDestructuringKind`, `DestructuringVariable` — AST model. - Opcodes `Destructure`, `SaveVariables`, `RestoreVariables` (`IrOpCode` 1.12) — binding extraction and lexical scoping, lowered by `IrLowerer` (1.54). - `VmEngine` (2.173/2.174) — `Destructure` semantics, `EnforceType` §3.4.2 coercion, `TryRelabelToDerivedNumeric` (PR 254 relabeling). - `EvaluationContext.TryGetDirectVariable` (2.36) — direct-binding probe for `SaveVariables`. ## 10. Collaborations - **Typed simple lets** (`let $v as xs:T := e`) — parsed at XP40+ as part of this slice; `EnforceType` applies XPath 4.0 §3.4.2 coercion when `IsXPath40` (untypedAtomic cast, numeric promotion, record coercion, derived-integer relabeling). - **Structural record types** — a `map(K,V)`/`record(...)` whole-pattern type validates the RHS shape (record patterns reject undeclared variables). - **Lexical scoping** — `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` wrap every `LetExpression` binding group; a trailing reference to a destructured variable outside the let's body raises XPST0008. (Caveat: emitted for `LetExpression` bindings only; XQuery full-FLWOR scoping has its own machinery.) ## 11. Consequences Benefits: single RHS evaluation; arity made explicit; map unpacks name their keys at the binding site. Liabilities: three binding semantics to learn (sequence rest / array strictness / map-by-name) — the drift table in §6 is the cheat sheet. Relabeling changes the *annotation*, not the datum (`42` → `xs:short` ✓; `2.5` → `xs:integer` is XPTY0004, never truncation). Save/Restore pairs are exception-unsafe by design (abandoned evaluations discard the frame with the whole stack — intentional). ## 12. Implementation Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs` (1.74), `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathAstNode.cs` (1.25), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrOpCode.cs` (1.12), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs` (1.54), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs` (2.173/2.174), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (2.36). Version gate: XPST0003 at `XPath31`; fully legal at `XPath40`. Regression: `VersionGateTests` (0.20, +10 rows), `ParserTests` (0.11, +6 AST tests). ## 13. Sample Code Additional executable catalog cases unpack invoice metadata and explicitly test a missing currency key: [main](../examples/destructuring-let/main.xpath) produces `INV-1042 / EUR`; [edge](../examples/destructuring-let/edge.xpath) returns missing currency cardinality `0`. These run at `XPath40` and verify default-mode refusal. Start with [the invoice chapter's practical migration pair](../worked-examples/invoice-to-erp/README.md#where-xpath-40-can-improve-readability): unpack invoice ID and currency from a metadata map to build a display label. Both complete expressions are supplied, engine-verified, and produce `INV-2026-1042 / EUR`. The 4.0 form requires explicit opt-in. The probes below cover the individual binding shapes. ~~~xquery let $($x, $y) := (1, 2, 3) return ($x, $y) (: → (1, (2,3)) — last variable takes the rest :) let $[$a, $b] := [3, 4, 5] return `a={$a} b={$b}` (: → "a=3 b=4" — surplus member 5 discarded :) let $[$a, $b] := [1] return $b (: → FOAY0001 :) let ${$name} := map {"name": "Braid"} return $name (: → "Braid" — key = variable local name :) let $($x as xs:short, $y) := (42, "ok") return ($x, $y) (: → (42 xs:short, "ok") — PR 254 relabeling; annotation changes, datum untouched :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Cost class: **small constant overhead**. One `Destructure` opcode per binding group plus one `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` frame pair — no per-item re-evaluation (the 3.1 un-hoisted idiom this replaces was potentially *more* expensive). No hot-path interaction known. No BenchmarkDotNet measurement exists for this feature as of 2026-10-10; the cost class is an implementation expectation, not a measurement. ## 15. Known Uses Practical case: `InvoiceReferenceGuideTests.InvoiceLabel_MigrationPairMatchesAndRequiresOptIn` executes both published label expressions and verifies XPST0003 in the default mode. This is a chapter-level example, separate from qt4tests gate evidence. qt4tests `prod-LetClause` **137/0/52** (52 skips = XQuery-only dependencies) and `fn-compare` collateral — both promoted into the conformance gate (223 sets) at landing. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_DestructuringLet_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_DestructuringSequence_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_DestructuringSequence_CoercionFailure_ThrowsXpty0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - Typed simple lets and §3.4.2 coercion (collaboration, §10) — own entry pending (Type system chapter). - Structural record types — own entry pending. - `fn:scan` — [experimental/fn-scan.md](../experimental/fn-scan.md) (same delivery wave, opposite tier). *Entry created 2026-10-10; updated 2026-10-11 with the verified invoice migration case (REQ-126).*

Intent Navigate JSON keys with path syntax, then unwrap the selected JNode for its value. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. data-model/jnode-template-boundary.md.text:
JNode model and template boundary

Deferred remainder; partial Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **JNode model and template boundary — Deferred remainder; partial Frozen 4.0.** Shipped delivery remains [PR #116](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/116), [revision 345ae58e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/345ae58e5f8e35d1b504aa0a7df250e3eaf88dd0). Scope review: 2026-10-12, engine 1.1.2, [revision 3c0bd599](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee). This reconciles the [original full-model exclusion](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) with partial delivered support. Primary references: [XDM generic nodes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-datamodel-40/Overview.html#generic-nodes), [XPath JNode types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-jnode-types), [jtree](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jtree), [jkey](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jkey), [jvalue](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jvalue), [XSLT built-in rules](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#built-in-rule). Immutable review sources: [XDM XML at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-datamodel-40/src/xpath-datamodel.xml), section `generic-nodes`, [function catalog](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml), and [XSLT source](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml). The review pin does not recover the missing historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Use shipped JSON navigation while keeping the broader generic-node type, identity and stylesheet contracts explicit. ## 3. Also Known As GNode means a generic node, collectively an XML node (XNode) or JSON wrapper node (JNode) in the reviewed draft. A plain map/array, a Bosak JNode wrapper and an IXdmNode XML adapter remain distinct values. ## 4. History / Supersedes REQ-118 originally excluded the full parallel model. REQ-123 subsequently delivered XdmJNode, jtree/jkey/jvalue, jnode type tests and navigation. That supersedes blanket wording that all JNode support is out of scope. The full unified model and JNode-specific stylesheet contracts remain uncertified. This review updates the original dossier rather than promoting the remainder. ## 5. Motivation A partner sends invoices as JSON. The application navigates array entries and nested keys to produce currency-labelled export rows. Parent context can help navigation, but consumers must not assume that XML-oriented node tests and identity operators already apply to every wrapper. ## 6. Language Alignment | Contract | Verified scope | |---|---| | Explicit jtree + child navigation + jvalue | Main, empty and reordered invoice reports work in Frozen 4.0 | | Plain map/array lookup | Portable 3.1 report produces the same rows for these inputs | | jkey on array children | 1-based positions `1|2` | | Parent navigation | Returns the enclosing invoice map; root parent empty | | jnode() test | Tested wrapper matches | | node() test on JNode | `false`; does not realize the draft's generic-node test | | xnode() on parsed XML | `XPST0051` in 3.1, 4.0 and experimental probes | | JNode identity with `is` | `XPTY0004`, even when both operands are the same wrapper | | Attribute axis on JNode | Empty in the tested case | | jvalue on a plain map | `XPTY0004`; unwrap only wrappers | Successful 4.0 cases retain the harness's default-3.1 refusal check. Error probes assert the declared marker, not a stage-specific diagnosis. This is scoped evidence, not exhaustive model conformance. ## 7. Applicability Choose 4.0 navigation when the host opts in and the wrapper operations meet the task. Retain portable map/array lookup for 3.1 integration. For stylesheet processing, unwrap JSON values and pass ordinary maps/arrays or construct XML explicitly; certify any additional template/model operation separately. ## 8. Structure The pinned model introduces a collective generic-node concept with node identity and order; `node()` covers GNodes and `xnode()` distinguishes XML nodes. Bosak stores JNode values separately from IXdmNode XML values. A wrapper records its value, entry key and parent; the root has no key/parent. Navigation support alone does not establish the common type and identity operators. ```xpath let $tree := jtree(map{'invoice':map{'id':'INV-1042'}}) return jvalue($tree/invoice/id/parent::*)?id ``` This is a complete parent-value operation; it is not an identity comparison or stylesheet rule dispatch. ## 9. Participants The host selects XPathCompatibility.XPath40. XdmJNode stores wrapper value/key/parent; the runtime navigates wrappers and the standard library creates/unwraps them. The invoice report formats scalar results. XML stylesheet source adapters remain a separate public integration surface. ## 10. Collaborations The 4.0 expression parses the full JSON, wraps the batch, navigates invoices and array members, then unwraps each invoice map. The portable expression traverses the same input by lookup. Both preserve invoice array order and keep currency with each total. They do not test universal equivalence of wrapper and map semantics. ## 11. Consequences The shipped feature is useful and should no longer be described as wholly absent. Confirmed broader gaps are node()/xnode() type alignment and JNode `is` identity. Default XSLT JNode rules, full generic-node ordering/union behavior and mixed-model operations are not certified here. No wrapper identity or stable map-key order is inferred from equal report strings. ## 12. Implementation Reviewed source: [XdmJNode.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Core/Xdm/XdmJNode.cs) stores Value/Key/Parent, while [VmEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) has JNode navigation/type branches but `EvaluateNodeComparison` requires IsNode operands. This explains the tested identity refusal. [TransformEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) and XML-oriented source APIs require separate review before claiming all draft JNode built-in template rules. Named existing evidence in [JNodeTests.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs): `Nav_ParentRoundTrip_ReturnsMapJNode`, `Nav_ChildOfArray_PositionKeyedJNodes`, `InstanceOf_Bare_MatchesAnyJNode`, `Nav_AttributeAxisOnJNode_IsEmpty`. Existing gate membership in [ConformanceRunner40.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) is `fn-jtree`, `fn-jkey`, `fn-jvalue`; membership is not a full generic-model gate. No gate is added or rerun in this documentation-only slice. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) adds eighteen checks, retaining the earlier `jnode-template-boundary-navigation` fixture. No engine/API/package changes. ## 13. Sample Code Complete invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or exchange conversion): ```json {"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]} ``` Complete Frozen 4.0 navigation report: ```xpath (: Partner invoice batch: navigate JNodes, unwrap each invoice map for reporting. :) let $tree := jtree(parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}')) return string-join($tree / invoices / * !
